# Compact JavaScript Entry Contract

The Awtsmoos can gather many module-rivers into one living scroll without confusing their source;
Awtsmoos.com should ask for that union at the browser doorway, while the server follows every local course.

## Direct source evidence

`ayzarim/awtsmoosDynamicServer/compactJs/flags.js` recognizes `compact=true`, `1`, `yes`, and boolean/number equivalents.

`static/FileResponseModes.js` compiles only explicit GET requests whose response is JavaScript, whose file ends in `.js`, and whose query requests compact mode. Ordinary static delivery is unchanged.

`compactJs/compiler.js` recursively follows local static imports and re-exports, folds literal local dynamic imports, preserves `import.meta.url` semantics, keeps bundled dynamic modules singleton, and emits public entry exports at the browser boundary.

`compactJs/paths.js` strips query/hash decorations before resolving local imports and mirrors browser public-root clamping. `/games/scripts/build/` and `/scripts/build/` are intentionally externalized vendor ESM prefixes rather than folded.

## Geelooy usage rule

Use `?compact=true` almost always on eligible browser **module entry URLs**, especially `<script type="module" src="...js">` and direct module entry navigation/fetches served by the Awtsmoos Dynamic server.

Do not mechanically append `?compact=true` to every internal static import specifier. Once an entry is requested compact, the compiler recursively folds those local dependencies. Adding the flag to every source import would create redundant compact entry points when a module is requested outside that graph and adds noise without increasing compaction inside the graph.

Do not apply compact mode to classic non-module scripts unless the entry has been proven compatible with module output. Do not apply it to external/vendor ESM paths the compiler intentionally externalizes.

Literal local dynamic imports do not need the query inside source when their compact entry already includes them; the compiler resolves them to the bundled namespace. Nonliteral runtime imports require separate evidence before conversion.

## Rollout gate

1. Run compactJs focused tests and real-entry sweep.
2. Census Geelooy HTML for `type=module` browser entry scripts lacking `compact=true`.
3. Exclude generated/debug/old/test pages and any route whose dynamic server mode is known incompatible.
4. Protect dirty/concurrent HTML before rewriting.
5. Convert clean/high-value public entries first using complete-file rewrites.
6. Verify normal Python/static serving still loads (query ignored by ordinary static servers) and, where an Awtsmoos Dynamic server is available, verify compact response syntax/runtime.

## NEXT_ACTION

Run compactJs tests, fresh shared player-shell acceptance, then rank public module entries and mobile UI risk together so import-performance work follows the same evidence-first preservation law as visual work.
